the structure of CPR-C2/NAPDH revealed the conformational change in the vicinity of the adp-ribose moiety of NADPH upon binding, and that this conformational change is responsible for the stereospecific substrate specificity of CPR-C2.
the crystal structures of CPR-C2/NAPDH complex revealed the conformational changes upon cofactor binding, which provide insight into substrate recognition by CPR-C2.
the crystal structures of CPR-C2/NAPDH and CPR-C2 apo form were determined, and the substrate specificity of CPR-C2 was explained by the cofactor induced conformational change.

the structural basis of CPR-C2, a ketone reductase that is useful for the production of ketopantonyl lactone, a precursor for vitamin B6.

CPR-C2 is a novel member of the aldo-ketoreductase superfamily that catalyses the stereospecific reduction of ketopantyolactone to d-pantoate.
we have elucidated the structure of CPR-C2, and the conformational changes of CPR-C2 upon NADPH-binding were discussed in detail.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CPR-C2 is a member of the aldo-ketoreductase superfamily and has a unique structure that enables it to reduce ketopantoyllactone to pantoyllactone in a highly specific manner.
the structure of CPR-C2 is similar to that of other aldo-keto-reductases, and that CPR-C2 adopts a triose-phosphates isomerase barrel core fold.
the structure of CPR-C2/NAPDH provides the structural basis of substrate specificity and that CPR-C2 mutants can be rationally designed for the industrial production of ketopantonyl lactone.
